decision.expected_measurable_effect: On the next complete execution of the single changed candidate, compared with baseline-replay: the final holding-window tip speed (scheduled 0.05 s window, same 0.02 m/s speed limit) differs measurably from the recorded 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s band, reported separately from terminal reach (terminal tip error against the 0.01 m tolerance), holding-window position error (0.01 m limit), and computation (per-update wall time and deadline misses). A reduction, an increase, or no measurable change are each informative for this bounded experiment.
decision.rationale: Accepted diagnosis (bound baseline-replay inventory, 35 retained updates, single execution): terminal reach is recorded as passed with terminal tip error 0.007642608585867386 m against the 0.01 m reach tolerance [fff8ec664f4de, f12f1083f9849], but terminal tip speed is recorded 0.6351726092425104 m/s [ffad04d70b19c] and the final holding window (6 selected samples, t 0.3-0.35 s [fa54c1ae23d4d, f5cdbebaa75dc]) records tip speed 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s [f952823a6555c, ff296c4b0c654] against the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit [f4ab3008c7e24], with holding position and sampled settling both recorded as failed [f5ba2ab7e1107, f641da2506e2e]. The retained recipe records terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 [f43a886f15dbe] and holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 [f7264b775e0bb], so the objective that produced this record contains no tip-speed cost term at all. Hypothesis: the recorded deviation is concentrated in tip speed, and an absent tip-speed penalty is a plausible contributor to that deviation, so positive values on these two terms should drive the sampled tip-speed band toward the 0.02 m/s settling limit. Relevance of this weight to this observation: these are the only two editable handles acting on squared tip speed, they are currently exactly zero so any positive value is an effective delta, and tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02 m/s, scheduling and structure remain unchanged. Expected effects, stated separately: holding speed (primary) - the scheduled holding-node sum should lower window tip speed below its current 0.635-1.581 m/s band; terminal reach - possible small degradation, since a terminal braking term can move the final approach while the terminal position margin under the 0.01 m tolerance is limited; holding position - secondary, plausibly improved if reduced speed reduces overshoot, but could be unchanged; computation - the objective gains terms and may raise iterations/nonconvexity, and nothing in the retained record indicates per-update wall time (already ~17 s against a 0.01 s control period [fb97841323574, ff74842fa741e, fc06e64bbb5d7]) would improve. Value selection is by mechanism only, since raw weight magnitudes are not calibrated against cost contributions or scaling; 0.01 on each weight is a bounded first choice, not a computed optimum, and no raw scalar objective will be compared across weights. Possible adverse effects: eroded reach margin, worse solve cost or deadline behaviour, and, with no causal attribution available, a null result cannot be read as proof that the term is irrelevant. Observations that would weaken the hypothesis: holding-window tip speed still ~0.6-1.6 m/s after the change; reach error crossing 0.01 m; terminal tip speed still far above 0.02 m/s; or deadline misses and per-update wall times materially worse than the baseline record. All other scientific fields remain fixed. A local 0.01 s projected-model comparison is omitted, not because it is unavailable but because a <=10 ms horizon probe cannot represent the 0.05 s settling window or closed-loop settling, so it would test neither the failing window quantity nor this hypothesis.

final_response.reasoning: Deferral, not adoption. The single authorized control change (holding_tip_speed_weight raised from the recorded baseline 0.0 [fe5f206322c2f] to 0.01 [ffa86380899d7], with terminal_tip_speed_weight also set positive [fdb85d027047b]) executed as a complete, valid run (complete true [fff684fc661de]; evaluation_validity 'valid' [ff37e5e0576b6]; solver_error_count 0 [ff1ac3503e552]; no force-bound violation [f008bb9364acd]; status 'evaluated' [fdd292670d74f]). It nevertheless lost the baseline's reach-only success (candidate terminal reach passed false [fb2196608130b] versus baseline official reach-task success true [ffee5636d7761]) and moved the ranked physical metrics in the worse direction: candidate holding-window maximum error 0.06521673847872775 m [fb551b0074893] with candidate-minus-baseline delta +0.00707863419299519 m [fd95239e6261c], and candidate sampled-settling maximum speed 2.2241210494240513 m/s [ffc6930742d22] versus the baseline holding-window maximum 1.5810152739742807 m/s [ff296c4b0c654]. Across both runs the 0.01 m position limit [f96748bb61be2], the 0.02 m/s speed limit [fec74be98dd03] and the 0.05 s settling window [fd898a5a0c311] remain unmet (sampled settling not passed [ff9225bf3aa43]; real-time not demonstrated [ff9345a5f7bef]), and the 10 ms control period [fd007fcdf7be2] is still missed on all 35 updates in each run [fc09ef600a821]. Those limits are reported as threshold observations, not as causes. No causal attribution is available: control_snapshots.json (full warm plans, optimizer iteration traces) is not retained, the candidate has no per-update inventory in this context, and a bounded projected-model probe of at most 0.01 s effective horizon cannot explain an entire settling failure, so any link between the computation record and the holding-window excursions stays at temporal co-occurrence. A valid completed workflow is therefore distinct from demonstrated design improvement, and no further parameter value or candidate is authorized.
